item.title: Apple’s China AI partner has had a rough ride
item.dc:creator: Lucia
item.description: Editor’s note: On Nov. 4, Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China, with Alibaba’s Qwen available in selected Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence experiences. The partnership crowns an unusually fast ascent for a model family launched in 2023. Hugging Face counted more than 2 billion Qwen downloads on its own Hub in the first […]
item.content:encoded:
Editor’s note: On Nov. 4, Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China, with Alibaba’s Qwen available in selected Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence experiences. The partnership crowns an unusually fast ascent for a model family launched in 2023. Hugging Face counted more than 2 billion Qwen downloads on its own Hub in the first seven months of 2026, well ahead of Google and Meta. But Qwen’s rise was anything but smooth: internal skepticism, fierce competition and senior departures shaped the model long before it became a global name.

First, Qwen Had to Win at Home

Qwen’s path to Apple did not begin as the story of an inevitable champion.

Alibaba introduced Tongyi Qianwen in April 2023, months after ChatGPT jolted China’s technology industry into a race to build large language models. It soon began releasing model weights publicly, gradually making open source central to Qwen’s strategy.

Even inside Alibaba, Qwen was not the automatic choice. Some teams kept using Meta’s Llama well into 2024, while Fliggy and Alibaba.com later experimented with DeepSeek’s R1. The model had to win over its own company before it could win over the wider market.

Open source became part of the answer. Developers fine-tuned Qwen, built derivatives and fed improvements back to the team, which credited that feedback in Qwen2.5’s expansion across language, coding and mathematics.

By late 2024, Qwen2.5 had begun winning over developers in China and the US — and more teams inside Alibaba.

Then DeepSeek arrived. Its R1 reasoning model raised the stakes across China’s AI industry, putting new pressure on rivals to deliver stronger reasoning at lower cost.

Alibaba founder Jack Ma repeatedly asked executives for updates on its development, according to The Information. In the final sprint, mattresses appeared beneath desks for power naps; some employees slept only a handful of hours during the final week.

Qwen3, released in April 2025, pushed into that new battleground with eight open models and hybrid reasoning, switching between a slower “thinking” mode for complex tasks and faster responses when deeper reasoning was unnecessary.

Its largest open model used a mixture-of-experts architecture, activating just 22 billion of 235 billion parameters at a time to cut inference costs. Reuters framed the launch as part of an intensifying Chinese AI race following DeepSeek’s rise.

Qwen’s Next Challenge Was Inside the Team

Over the next year, Qwen kept expanding its model family and developer reach. But by early 2026, the pressure around the team was no longer just technical.

In March, technical leader Junyang Lin abruptly announced his departure with three words: “Bye my beloved Qwen.” Post-training chief Bowen Yu also left, following senior researcher Binyuan Hui earlier that year.

Alibaba didn’t publicly detail Lin’s reasons. 36Kr reported tensions over a proposed reorganization, team boundaries, hiring and computing resources.

At an emergency all-hands meeting, researchers questioned why paying Alibaba Cloud customers could secure computing capacity while Qwen’s own team remained short of resources.

Management acknowledged communication problems while saying the changes were meant to strengthen, not weaken, Qwen.

The episode pointed to a broader tension facing frontier AI labs: cutting-edge models demand centralized capital and vast computing resources, while top research teams often rely on autonomy and fast decision-making.

Alibaba responded by tightening coordination. In June, it created Token Foundry, consolidating key model-development teams under CEO Eddie Wu.

By September, longtime Qwen researcher Dayiheng Liu had been appointed head of the Qwen large language model project, bringing more clarity after several rounds of reorganization.

Beyond the Model Race

Qwen had grown beyond a model family into a broader stack: foundation models for language, coding and multimodal tasks; Alibaba Cloud’s Model Studio for developers and enterprises; and consumer products such as the Qwen App.

That breadth mattered to Apple. After evaluating Chinese AI providers including Baidu, Tencent, ByteDance, Alibaba and DeepSeek, Apple chose Alibaba as a partner for Apple Intelligence in China.

By August 2026, Apple had also trained a China-specific model with Alibaba’s support, while the approved setup incorporated Qwen.

Alibaba is backing that push at group scale. In February 2025, it pledged at least 380 billion yuan ($53 billion) over three years specifically for AI and cloud infrastructure — more than it had spent on the two areas over the previous decade.

Its broader AI investment strategy also covers foundation models and AI-native applications, as well as integrating AI across existing businesses. By May 2026, Alibaba said its spending would exceed the original 380 billion yuan plan.

The Apple deal marks a new phase. The harder part may be keeping Qwen fast, focused and inventive as the machinery around it gets bigger.

item.title: Tencent expands Hy4 inference capacity tenfold as WorkBuddy demand surges
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Tencent said on November 5 that it had expanded inference capacity for its Hy4 model tenfold after heavy demand on WorkBuddy caused many users to reach their usage limits on the first day. The company also increased free usage allowances and said it would continue adjusting resources to meet demand. According to materials provided by […]
item.content:encoded:
Tencent said on November 5 that it had expanded inference capacity for its Hy4 model tenfold after heavy demand on WorkBuddy caused many users to reach their usage limits on the first day. The company also increased free usage allowances and said it would continue adjusting resources to meet demand.

According to materials provided by Tencent, Hy4 ranked second among Chinese models on Artificial Analysis’ intelligence index, behind Kimi K3.1 Pro. It also ranked 13th overall and first among open-weight models on Agent Arena. Tencent cited an Artificial Analysis benchmark cost of about $0.78 per task.

Tencent released Hy4 on November 4, adding visual understanding and expanding pre-training and post-training compared with its preview version. The company said the upgrade improved instruction following, long-context comprehension, and extended agent workflows. [TechNode reporting]

item.title: DeepSeek plans official plugin marketplace as Harness daily users reach 1.54 million
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: DeepSeek plans to build an official plugin marketplace for Harness, making it easier for developers to distribute plugins and users to discover them. The team is also preparing a creator support program covering token incentives, technical exchanges, and recommendations, alongside improvements to plugin API stability, compatibility, and security. Harness had 1.54 million daily active users […]
item.content:encoded:
DeepSeek plans to build an official plugin marketplace for Harness, making it easier for developers to distribute plugins and users to discover them. The team is also preparing a creator support program covering token incentives, technical exchanges, and recommendations, alongside improvements to plugin API stability, compatibility, and security.

Harness had 1.54 million daily active users as of November 4, counting users accessing the service through DeepSeek’s official API. Third-party plugins had reached about 35,000, with roughly 60% of active users having created or installed at least one. [IT Home, in Chinese]

item.title: Ant launches Ling-3.2-flash multimodal model with million-token context
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Ant Group released Ling-3.2-flash on November 5, adding a native multimodal model that accepts text, images, and video. The model has 560 billion total parameters, activates 25 billion per inference step, and supports a one-million-token context window. Ant says the model focuses on complex visual understanding, multistep agent tasks, 3D understanding and interaction, and medical […]
item.content:encoded:
Ant Group released Ling-3.2-flash on November 5, adding a native multimodal model that accepts text, images, and video. The model has 560 billion total parameters, activates 25 billion per inference step, and supports a one-million-token context window.

Ant says the model focuses on complex visual understanding, multistep agent tasks, 3D understanding and interaction, and medical multimodal applications. It is available through an online chat interface and APIs compatible with OpenAI and Anthropic protocols, with free access for the first two weeks after launch. [Ant Ling]

item.title: Sand.ai raises $200 million ahead of MAGI-2 video model release
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Chinese video-generation company Sand.ai announced a $200 million Series A+ funding round on November 5. The company said the investment gave it unicorn status and brought its fundraising this year to $300 million across three rounds. Cornerstone Capital and Wangsu Science & Technology jointly led the round. Sand.ai will use the proceeds for video-model research, […]
item.content:encoded:
Chinese video-generation company Sand.ai announced a $200 million Series A+ funding round on November 5. The company said the investment gave it unicorn status and brought its fundraising this year to $300 million across three rounds.

Cornerstone Capital and Wangsu Science & Technology jointly led the round. Sand.ai will use the proceeds for video-model research, training and inference infrastructure, product development, and international expansion. It also plans to release the full version of MAGI-2, a larger video-generation model built on a mixture-of-experts architecture, soon. [Jiemian, in Chinese]

item.title: Baidu Tests a New Way to Train Robotaxis
item.dc:creator: Lucia
item.description: SHENZHEN, China — Nov. 3: Baidu’s Apollo unit unveiled Apollo World, an agent-driven multimodal world model for physical AI, at its AI Day event in Shenzhen. Why it matters: Apollo defines a world model by two requirements: causality and interactivity — the future follows the past, and the world responds to the vehicle’s actions. What […]
item.content:encoded:
SHENZHEN, China — Nov. 3: Baidu’s Apollo unit unveiled Apollo World, an agent-driven multimodal world model for physical AI, at its AI Day event in Shenzhen.

  • The model is already being used to test and validate Apollo Go as the driverless ride-hailing service expands into more markets, according to the company.

Why it matters: Apollo defines a world model by two requirements: causality and interactivity — the future follows the past, and the world responds to the vehicle’s actions.

  • “A world model is not a painter that generates videos, but an examiner of autonomous-driving safety,” said Liang Wang, chief architect of Baidu’s Intelligent Driving Group.

What happened: Apollo World creates a closed-loop virtual environment where AI-driven cars and pedestrians react to the vehicle, while simulated camera and lidar data feed back into the AI driver.

  • It can test complete trips, not just isolated maneuvers.
    • “Apollo World focuses more on closed-loop simulation of complete tasks,” said Ze Yang, Baidu IDG distinguished architect and world-model lead.
  • The system aims to cut costly road testing.
    • Each model iteration requires, on average, more than 700,000 kilometers of road testing. Apollo World was trained on more than 1 billion high-value frames.
  • The closed loop uses both camera and lidar data.
    • In response to a TechNode question, Wang said the model fuses the two, while Yang said combining them gives the system more information than vision alone.
  • Safety is a key goal. Wang said virtual testing helps catch problems before less-predictable end-to-end models are deployed at scale.

The big picture: Robotaxi competition is increasingly playing out across markets, with companies racing to adapt driverless systems to different cities, regulations and driving environments.

  • Apollo Go built its base in China, where its mainland operations are now 100% fully driverless.
  • It has logged more than 23 million rides and 240 million fully driverless kilometers across its operations.
  • Overseas, it has launched fully driverless commercial rides in Dubai, with testing or expansion underway in London, Switzerland, Hong Kong, Abu Dhabi and South Korea.
  • The push comes as Waymo, WeRide and Pony.ai also expand abroad, intensifying competition to establish robotaxi services in new markets.

item.title: ZTE denies smartphone sale rumors hinting at ByteDance involvement
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: ZTE has denied reports that it plans to transfer its smartphone business into a joint venture with a major internet company and local state-owned investors, amid online speculation identifying ByteDance as the potential partner. ZTE told The Paper on November 3 that the reports were seriously inconsistent with the facts and said it reserved the […]
item.content:encoded:
ZTE has denied reports that it plans to transfer its smartphone business into a joint venture with a major internet company and local state-owned investors, amid online speculation identifying ByteDance as the potential partner. ZTE told The Paper on November 3 that the reports were seriously inconsistent with the facts and said it reserved the right to take legal action.

The reported proposal involved packaging ZTE’s handset operations into a new venture. While the media report did not name the internet company, social media discussion pointed to ByteDance, which already works with ZTE on AI smartphones.

The companies jointly developed the Nubia NaviX Ultra, launched on September 16 with the Doubao Phone Assistant. The device integrates system-level AI agents designed to execute tasks across applications. [The Paper, in Chinese]

item.title: Oracle reportedly cancels $7 billion Tencent AI chip lease under US pressure
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Oracle has canceled a five-year agreement to lease advanced AI chips to Tencent after pressure from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on November 4. The deal, valued at approximately $7 billion, would have given Tencent access to around 100,000 advanced AI chips across Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia. US officials raised concerns […]
item.content:encoded:
Oracle has canceled a five-year agreement to lease advanced AI chips to Tencent after pressure from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on November 4. The deal, valued at approximately $7 billion, would have given Tencent access to around 100,000 advanced AI chips across Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia.

US officials raised concerns about the arrangement with Oracle, according to the report. Tencent also received visits from senior officials in Guangdong who asked it to support Chinese chips. Reuters said it could not independently verify the report, and Oracle, Tencent and the White House did not respond to its requests for comment. [Reuters]
